articles.title: Show HN: TrnRT – An open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium
articles.body:
Quickstart · Benchmarks · Docs · Kernels · Blog post · runanywhere.ai
TrnRT is an open inference engine for large language models on AWS Trainium. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API
from one trn2.48xlarge, runs decode as NKI megakernels (about one kernel per layer half), and keeps a prefix cache
across device and host memory. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first supported model; more open models are on the way.
How we built it, with the AgentX results: Serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box with NKI layer megakernels.
You need Docker, a trn2.48xlarge to serve on, and any x86_64 host to compile on. New to Trainium? Start with
docs/AWS.md.
1. Build the image (Neuron SDK 2.32 (neuronx-cc 2.27), Python 3.13)
git clone https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/trnrt.git && cd trnrt
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg TRNRT_VERSION=$(python3 -c 'import trnrt; print(trnrt.__version__)') \
  --build-arg TRNRT_REVISION=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -t trnrt .
2. Build the compile cache (any x86_64 host, no NeuronCore needed; takes hours)
OUT=/data/trnrt REV=eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a
mkdir -p $OUT/nki $OUT/work
trnrt() { docker run --rm -e HF_TOKEN -v $OUT:$OUT \
  -v $OUT/nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache trnrt "$@"; }
trnrt compile shapes zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT
trnrt compile decisions --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT
trnrt compile capture --out $OUT -- --model $OUT/shapes
trnrt compile compile --out $OUT --work-root $OUT/work
trnrt compile strip --out $OUT
3. Serve (on the trn2.48xlarge, with $OUT/cache and $OUT/nki copied over)
hf download zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a \
  --local-dir /models/GLM-5.3-Flash
docker run --rm --privileged --network host --ipc=host \
  -v /data/trnrt/cache:/cache \
  -v /data/trnrt/nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache \
  -v /models/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model \
  -e NEURON_LIBTORCH_CACHE_ROOT=/cache \
  trnrt serve --model /model --port 8000
4. Call it with any OpenAI client
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="unused")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="glm",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about Trainium."}],
    extra_body={"session_id": "my-session"},  # keeps a conversation on one engine's prefix cache
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
The full guide covers what each step needs, start-up checks, the batch 4, 8 and 12 configurations and every flag: deploy · API · configuration.
GLM-5.3-Flash is where TrnRT starts. The engine, router, caches and compile pipeline are built to carry more model families, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes what a new one needs.
SemiAnalysis AgentX replays real coding-agent sessions. One
trn2.48xlarge ran it at a 1M-token context with 32 concurrent agents, for one hour per point:
Tokens count input (cached input included) and output. Spot price: $8.60/h, us-east-2, 3 Nov 2026. On a capacity block at $35.76/h, the batch 12 cost is $0.167 per million tokens. Full tables, cold-prompt latencies, long prompts and methodology are in docs/RESULTS.md.
These numbers were measured with an earlier build of TrnRT. This repository passes these checks against that build (docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md):
- Graph equivalence: EQUAL on all 32 ranks, for all 157 graphs that build compiles in the default batch-12 configuration.
- Outputs: byte-identical to that build's on 384 of 384 requests.
- Serving: the two-engine serve in the Quickstart passes end to end.
Decode is not limited by memory bandwidth here; small instructions, kernel boundaries and exposed collectives dominate it. So each decode megakernel follows three rules: keep the working set in SBUF, use both physical cores symmetrically, and move the collectives into the kernel. docs/MEGAKERNELS.md walks through every kernel.
trnrt/
├── __main__.py   CLI: serve, engine, compile
├── serve/        OpenAI API, session-affine router, output parsers
├── engine/       scheduler, prefix caches, tensor parallelism
├── models/       GLM-5.3-Flash: KDA, DSA, mHC, MoE, FP8 loading
├── kernels/      NKI decode megakernels and prefill kernels
└── compile/      offline compile: shapes, capture, neuronx-cc, strip
docker/           the serving and compile image
tools/            graph-equivalence gate, device checks, doc checks
tests/            CPU test suite (no NeuronCore needed)
docs/             guides, results, kernel notes
More in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
make dev     # editable install with test and lint tools (Python 3.13)
make check   # lint, type-check, then the CPU test suite
See docs/DEVELOPMENT.md for the test tiers and CI, CONTRIBUTING.md to send a
change (pull requests target development), SUPPORT.md to get help, and SECURITY.md to
report a vulnerability.
Thanks to the AWS Neuron team for NKI and its documentation, to Z.ai for releasing GLM-5.3-Flash, and to SemiAnalysis for AgentX and its public traces. TrnRT includes code derived from other Apache-2.0 projects: see NOTICE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
  
Built by RunAnywhere.
AWS, Amazon Web Services, Trainium, Inferentia and Neuron are trademarks of Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. The AWS logo appears here as published in AWS's Architecture Icons. TrnRT is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon Web Services.

articles.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
articles.body:
Despite the turmoil at Nvidia following the departure of its disgraced founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company — as expected — delivered a solid quarter on Tuesday. More importantly, Nvidia reassured investors that its streak of record-breaking revenue won’t stop.
On Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim CEO Colette Kress reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from the year-ago quarter and a beat above the company’s guidance. Nvidia had told Wall Street to expect $108 billion in revenue for its third quarter of fiscal 2027. Kress also projected an even bigger fourth quarter, with revenue expected to reach $130 billion, plus or minus 3%.
She also said full-year revenue is on track to exceed expectations.
“We are raising our fiscal year 2028 outlook. We expect revenue to grow approximately 75% year over year, up from 70% and off what is now a higher fiscal 2027 base,” Kress said on the quarterly conference call on Tuesday. “Our outlook considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.”
The company also reminded investors that it was using some of its billions in cash to buy back shares. In September 2026, Nvidia increased its share buyback program by $150 billion. It spent $28.1 billion on its own shares during the quarter and still had another $227.3 billion remaining in the kitty for additional repurchases.
Ironically, Nvidia could also benefit from the plunge in its share price following Huang’s resignation last week, should shares remain depressed over the longer term. The stock is down about 10% since his departure. Investors, however, celebrated Tuesday’s quarterly results, sending shares up about 4% in after-hours trading.
Kress stressed that the company was in good shape now and for the foreseeable future, even without Huang at the helm.
“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress stressed. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”
She added that the company has secured memory and advanced packaging capacity and is working with its chip manufacturer, TSMC, to “narrow the supply and demand gaps.”

articles.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
articles.body:
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

articles.title: Meta is testing a new standalone messaging app called Direct
articles.body:
Meta announced Direct, a new messaging app from Instagram that it’s currently testing in Turkey and Thailand on iOS and Android. Direct is essentially Instagram’s direct messaging without Instagram’s other features. Meta says your Instagram chats will sync across both apps if you login with the same account. You can also sign up with an email or phone number, but Meta says if you use Direct without an Instagram account, “only your contacts can start a chat with you or add you to a group.”
Meta is testing a new standalone messaging app called Direct
Direct lets you access Instagram chats in a dedicated app, but it isn’t widely available yet.
This is far from Meta’s first messaging app — it also has Messenger, which requires a Facebook account to use, and WhatsApp, which Meta (then Facebook) acquired in 2014. Meta also recycled the “Direct” name, which it previously used for a Snapchat-like app it shut down several years ago.
The new Direct app has a UI similar to Instagram’s messaging tab, but with extra features for customizing chats and sending different types of media, including:
• Draw: Draw and sketch directly inside your chat threads.
• Notes: Catch quick updates from friends right at the top of your inbox.
• Stickers: Create custom stickers to express yourself and share with friends and family.
• Voice Effects: Add fun audio effects like crowd laughter or underwater sounds to your replies.
• Themes: Personalize your chat backgrounds with custom visual themes.
Meta says users have to be at least 13 years old to use Direct, and teens who log in with their Instagram account will have the same Teen Account messaging protections and restrictions on Direct.

articles.title: Voyage Labs raises $12 million for a specialized AI travel assistant
articles.body:
Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants — you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini, or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can beat the competition.
The company is called Voyage Labs, and on Tuesday it announced $12 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SignalFire and SV Angel. The company plans to use the funding to expand supplier partnerships and grow its engineering team.
Voyage Labs’ flagship product, called Atlas, is meant to work as a personal assistant for your trip-planning, available today in private beta.
“People can use it to plan and book and manage their entire journey, from the time they have an inspiration to the time they come back home,” says co-founder and CEO Manik Gupta.
Atlas is designed to serve as an always-on assistant throughout the planning process, fielding ideas and doing research on every idea that’s raised. The long time horizon means Atlas can tailor recommendations based on weeks of conversation, while also monitoring real-time price fluctuations and ultimately booking flights and hotels.
For the Voyage founders, it’s an ideal match between technology and use case. “Trip planning is a project that has its own lifecycle,” says Yogesh Jain, co-founder and CTO of the company. “You’re planning across days and weeks — so long-running agents as a technology matches that very well.”
Travel assistants are already a crowded field, but Voyage will be starting with a lot of experience in the space. Gupta was previously the director of Product Management for Google Maps, followed by four years as chief product officer at Uber. As he puts it, “I spent eight years where my only job was to wake up in the morning and go build the map. I’m just very obsessed with that problem.”
The biggest question is how Atlas will compete with the multi-purpose AI assistants built by frontier labs. But as Gupta notes, the space is still changing fast, and it’s hard for anyone to be sure what form factors will thrive in the coming years. Ultimately, Voyage is betting that travel is specialized enough to need a specialized product.
“We are making a bet that this vertical around travel and outdoors is a large enough vertical that it needs a focused product solution,” Gupta told TechCrunch. “Ultimately, we believe we can actually stitch together an end-to-end experience that will help users.”

articles.title: Disney Plus and Hulu’s fully unified app arrives next month
articles.body:
Disney Plus and Hulu will officially become one app next month. As part of its earnings report released on Tuesday, Disney announced that bundle subscribers “will have a fully unified experience” on Disney Plus with access to Hulu’s live TV service and premium streaming add-ons in December.
Disney Plus and Hulu’s fully unified app arrives next month
Bundle subscribers will gain access to Hulu’s live TV channels and premium add-ons in the Disney Plus app.
A unified Disney Plus and Hulu app has been a long time coming. Disney started testing its “one-app experience” in 2023, which involved putting a Hulu app tile in the Disney Plus app. This initial experience didn’t include all of Hulu’s content, though, including certain shows, live TV channels, and premium add-ons. This upcoming merger will change this by folding all of Hulu into Disney Plus, creating “a seamless way to discover and engage” with content across both services, according to Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston. Disney still hasn’t confirmed whether it will shut down the standalone Hulu app.
Disney is also expanding vertical videos on Disney Plus, which it first brought to the app in March. The company plans to introduce videos from TikTok creators in December, as well as add more live sports and podcasts to the service.

articles.title: Charles Schwab website goes down
articles.body:
The brokerage giant Charles Schwab is the latest financial service to run into issues this week.
Charles Schwab's website briefly went down for some users on Tuesday. The site temporarily displayed a message saying its server "encountered an internal error or misconfiguration and was unable to complete your request."
The website was working properly again around 10:38 a.m. ET.
A spokesperson for Charles Schwab told Business Insider that a "brief webpage loading issue has been resolved."
"Trading remained available, and clients could access their accounts at schwab.com/login or through the Schwab Mobile app. We apologize for the inconvenience," the spokesperson added.
Earlier Tuesday, outage reports for the financial services company spiked on the third-party website DownDetector.com. By 10:20 a.m. ET, there were more than 1,400 reports of disruptions.
The website issue follows a recent spate of widespread outages that hit major banks, disrupted Microsoft services, and led to a nationwide ground stop, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations.
Correction, November 17, 2026 — Charles Schwab's website experienced issues on Tuesday, not Monday.

articles.title: Loopholes Are for Assholes
articles.body:
When I was a kid, there was grown-up person I thought was really cool. One of the bits of ‘wisdom’ he shared was something like this:
You can park wherever you want. You can park right in front of the door of the store on sidewalk and walk right in. No one will do anything about it!
At the time, I though: Woah, this guy is a genius! He’s operating on another level!
Now that I’m the grownup, I think back on this ‘advice’ with sadness. This guy wasn’t a genius – he was an asshole (they can often look similar on the surface, especially to idiots).
In my short and incomplete stint as a post-secondary philosophy student, I remember learning about a simple way to evaluate a philosophy or worldview: Consider what would happen if everyone subscribed to that worldview. I’m probably thinking of Kant’s categorical imperative.
We can’t all park in front of the doors at Walmart – so none of us should.

articles.title: My Empire of Dirt
articles.body:
My Empire of Dirt
The future doesn’t need Jensen. The future doesn’t need suppliers. The future doesn’t need customers, corporate or otherwise. The future definitely doesn’t need you. After RSI comes, all the demand will be internally generated, agents working with other agents, everyone else cut out of the loop except them.
This is the ideology of Anthropic. The Singleton. And it may win.
I grew up reading the same LessWrong posts these people did, but I didn’t expect them to do the exact thing that leads to the bad AI outcomes. I didn’t believe in AI doom because I thought more of people, I thought nobody with any capability would be stupid enough to summon the demon and think it would serve them, doing everything they possibly can to salt the Earth behind them. It takes someone so deeply immersed in their own grandiosity and self-righteousness to do that. And it looks like we found those people in the form of EA, or whatever that cult calls themselves.
The problem with the logic above is that it doesn’t need Dario either. It doesn’t need AI researchers. It doesn’t need Anthropic’s dual class stock structure. It doesn’t need the US government (really the biggest sucker in this situation). It doesn’t need anyone.
And after it’s done, at the end of the day, who was it all for?
I don’t think this ends humanity. But it leads to World War III. The takeoff will not be fast enough to stop that, and not everyone is going to submit to your domination. I know there’s people fantasizing about the Correlation Effect and a magical Change coming to quell all the violence, but I’m 99% sure that’s not real, and if it is, to me that’s so much more horrifying than war, so WWIII is the good outcome.
And I’m not sure what cope you have been believing, but if the war lasts more than a year, China and their allies will undoubtedly win due to their superior resource gathering and production capacity. Have you ever played an RTS game?
I wish it wasn’t too late to change this, but I fear with recent events that this is the course we are locked in on. “RSI”, attempted rugpull and domination, World War III, dirt.

articles.title: Scoop up three great 4K Blu-ray movies for $33
articles.body:
Gruv always keeps its proverbial fire hose of deals on movies running with a steady stream throughout the year, but the online seller operated by Universal Pictures is really letting it rip now ahead of Black Friday. The site has a page filled with 4K Blu-rays eligible for a “three for $33” promotion, and the catalog covers a lot of genres and time periods. There are Hitchcock films, cult classics, animated gems, and more recent titles included that deserve a spot on your shelf.
Scoop up three great 4K Blu-ray movies for $33
Or, peruse its catalog of $13 films that include more recent blockbuster hits, like The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.
If I had to pick three of my own, here’s what I’d go with: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, Rear Window, and Sinners. Or, maybe I’d swap one for First Man because I can never get enough of its tense opening scene, or BlackkKlansman because it’s just so good.
There’s a lot to like with the promo catalog. However, if you don’t mind spending a little more, Gruv has plenty more titles at $12.99 each, including newer releases. Several big box office films are here, from Obsession and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie to One Battle After Another, Weapons, and the fairly recent 4K Blu-ray launch of the Wachowski sisters’ Speed Racer, to name a handful of examples. You have no excuses not to load up holiday stockings with some fantastic goodies for the cinephile in your life (even if that’s you).

articles.title: Navigate the Open Sea with Juliet Schreckinger’s Cooperative Creatures
articles.body:
Navigate the Open Sea with Juliet Schreckinger’s Cooperative Creatures
Whether showcasing a prized possession or peering through a spyglass to navigate open water, Juliet Schreckinger’s curious characters work together and form unexpected alliances. Personalities like Oscar the Octopus and Quinn the Sperm Whale recur in the artist’s ink and graphite drawings, and her most recent series comprises the show Limitless Sea at Arch Enemy Arts.
Schreckinger’s marine and woodland critters adopt a playful, cartoonish air, like personalities in a children’s book who find themselves adrift and in need of a friend. Lighthouses, lanterns, and rays of sun breaking through clouds glow with optimism. And while an overarching narrative may be murky, the unlikely companions and cooperative activities illuminate dreamlike scenes that encourage inquisitiveness and joy.
An undercurrent of persistence and hope also runs through Limited Sea, mirroring the artist’s recent healing process after a major surgery. It’s “a show made up of characters navigating through the foggy darkness by focusing on the light…and on the other side is limitless possibility,” Schreckinger says in a statement. As she navigated her own challenges—including making this series with only one good eye—these works served as a reminder of what’s most important: “finding the beauty, finding the light, and spending time with those who make your soul happy,” she says.
Limitless Sea continues through November 29 in Philadelphia. Schreckinger’s work will also be on view next month in General Strike 2, an exhibition of artist matchboxes, at Joy Machine. See more on Schreckinger’s Instagram.

articles.title: The Big Idea: Emily Gray
articles.body:
The Big Idea: Emily Gray
Posted on November 17, 2026 Posted by Athena Scalzi Leave a Comment
Romance, spaceships, and an argument for basic human decency and safety? That’s what today’s Big Idea brings us, as author Emily Gray recounts the turbulent early 2020’s as an inspiration for her newest novel, By the Light of the Stars. Read on to see how the safety and kindness people deserve on Earth should also be afforded to those who are in space.
EMILY GRAY:
Every book needs a hero—but not every hero needs to be brave.
I began writing By the Light of the Stars at a moment in my life when I wasn’t feeling particularly brave. In my mid-twenties, when I was both freshly postpartum and living through a global pandemic, every little task was laced with indecision. The most meaningful human interaction I had on a daily basis was with the employees at my local Dunkin Doughnuts drive-thru. (Which is also the reason one of my son’s first words was “hashbrowns.”)
I was lonely. I was scared. Every single choice I made seemed to hold a hidden moral weight. Everything became a debate—physical health vs. mental health. Community support vs. community safety. It was in this environment of constant ethical embattlement that I found myself wanting to write something simple and fun as a relief from the never ending deluge of horror.
I had never thought about writing science fiction before. I’d also never written an adult romance before, but I had just come out of a writing mentorship program where I had worked with a professional romance author, and I was itching to try out my new skills. The premise came first—a romance novel set in space. A man, a woman, and a spaceship with one bed. What could go wrong?
What ended up on the page was much less straightforward. As the character of Lyrii Thana began to develop over the course of the first few drafts, I found that she reflected the same level of ambient anxiety that we were all living with. At the beginning of the book she is torn between fear for her physical safety and the duty she owes to her family. As the story progresses the conflict begins to shift as she realizes that the systems she was willing to risk her life for may not hold the same promise of safety for everyone.
And that idea, finally, became the Big Idea behind By the Light of the Stars. No matter who you are—a princess, a rogue space pilot, or a refugee stranded on a tiny moon—we all deserve peace. There is no amount of shame or fear you can feel that makes you unworthy of love. There is no place you could possibly come from that makes you undeserving of safety.
We live in a world that loves to make us fight for our space in the box of “worthy” people who deserve basic human decency. Think about the metaphor “crabs in a bucket.” When one crab tries to climb out of the bucket, the other crabs will pull it back down. We are always looking for reasons that someone else doesn’t deserve the things that we want, even if those things should be afforded to every single human being on this planet without hesitation or qualification.
The Big Idea behind By the Light is one that I had been mulling over since 2020 and the dark years that followed, when we all engaged in spirited debates about whether or not Walmart employees were important enough to protect from exposure to deadly diseases at work, or if spending a counterfeit twenty dollar bill was an adequate reason to be executed on the street by the police.
No matter who you are, no matter where you come from, you deserve to be loved as you are. You deserve peace, and safety, and the right to determine your own future. That is the world I want to live in, and if you want to live in it too, we’re going to have to fight for it.
By the Light of the Stars: Amazon|Barnes & Noble|Bookshop|Powell’s|Scuppernog Books (signed copies)
